question: A 32-year-old woman presents to her primary care provider complaining of a psoriatic flare that has worsened over the past 2 days. The patient states that her psoriasis is normally well-controlled. She also complains of some fatigue and states that she has recently developed pain and tenderness in the joints of her hands with the right hand being more tender than the left. Her hands are stiff in the morning, and sometimes her fingers swell up. She attributes these changes to her new job where she constantly uses her hands to manufacture cabinets. Physical exam reveals plaques with silvery scale on her elbows and knees. The distal joints of her right hand are mildly swollen and the nails on both hands appear pitted. What is the most likely pathogenesis of her joint pain?

options.opa: Local invasive infection of the joint space
options.opc: Autoantibodies to the Fc portion of IgG
options.opd: Deposition of crystals in the joint space
options.ope: Release of TNF and activation of RANKL pathway

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Psoriasis flare" -> "Joint pain in hands" -> "Morning stiffness and finger swelling" -> "Pitted nails" -> "Plaques with silvery scale on elbows and knees" -> "Likely psoriatic arthritis" -> "Autoantibodies to the Fc portion of IgG" -> 85% CHAIN: "Repetitive use of hands in new job" -> "Joint pain and tenderness in hands" -> "Morning stiffness and finger swelling" -> "Pitted nails" -> "Plaques with silvery scale on elbows and knees" -> "Likely psoriatic arthritis" -> "Autoantibodies to the Fc portion of IgG" -> 85%
enhanced_information: The most likely pathogenesis of the joint pain in this patient with psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis is the presence of autoantibodies to the Fc portion of IgG, supported by the association between psoriasis, joint pain, morning stiffness, finger swelling, pitted nails, and plaques with silvery scale. The evidence paths confirm the link between psoriatic arthritis and autoantibodies.
analysis: The most likely pathogenesis of joint pain in this patient with psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis is the presence of autoantibodies to the Fc portion of IgG. This is supported by the association between psoriasis, joint pain, morning stiffness, finger swelling, pitted nails, and plaques with silvery scale, which are characteristic features of psoriatic arthritis.
